title: Gate clauses for Tseitin encoding
statement: For a gate $g$ and a natural-number variable $z$, its Tseitin encoding is a conjunctive normal form over natural-number variables defined by the following clauses, with a literal $(v,	ext{true})$ denoting $v$ and $(v,	ext{false})$ denoting its negation. A zero-argument AND gate gives the unit clause $(z,	ext{true})$, while a zero-argument OR or NOT gate gives $(z,	ext{false})$. For one argument $j$, AND and OR give the clauses $(z,	ext{false})\vee(j,	ext{true})$ and $(z,	ext{true})\vee(j,	ext{false})$; NOT gives $(z,	ext{true})\vee(j,	ext{true})$ and $(z,	ext{false})\vee(j,	ext{false})$. For two arguments $j,k$, AND gives the four clauses $(z,	ext{false})\vee(j,\text{false})\vee(k,\text{true})$, $(z,\text{false})\vee(j,\text{true})\vee(k,\text{false})$, $(z,\text{false})\vee(j,\text{true})\vee(k,\text{true})$, and $(z,\text{true})\vee(j,\text{false})\vee(k,\text{false})$; OR gives $(z,\text{false})\vee(j,\text{true})\vee(k,\text{true})$, $(z,\text{true})\vee(j,\text{true})\vee(k,\text{false})$, $(z,\text{true})\vee(j,\text{false})\vee(k,\text{true})$, and $(z,\text{true})\vee(j,\text{false})\vee(k,\text{false})$; NOT gives $(z,\text{true})\vee(j,\text{true})\vee(k,\text{true})$, $(z,\text{true})\vee(j,\text{true})\vee(k,\text{false})$, $(z,\text{true})\vee(j,\text{false})\vee(k,\text{true})$, and $(z,\text{false})\vee(j,\text{false})\vee(k,\text{false})$. Every other argument list gives the empty CNF.
hypotheses_covered: A natural-number variable $z$ and a gate $g$
The cases cover gate kind and argument-list length, including the empty-CNF default for all other lengths
